To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a new way to use the symmetry of viruses to find a starting point to determine the structure of a virus using the x-ray free electron laser.
we can use the near-symmetric nature of the virus diffraction patterns to obtain the sign of the expansion coefficients of the diffraction volume.

the X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) will enable the determination of the structures of individual biological particles in the absence of crystallization, that the structures of viruses can be determined by using their near-symmetry to find a first approximate structure, and that the structures of individual viruses can be determined from a small number of diffraction images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) as a tool for determining the three dimensional structures of biological macromolecules.
the application of the X-ray free-electron laser to the structure determination of individual viruses.
the application of the theory of perturbation to the determination of the structures of viruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in principle, it is possible to determine the structure of a biological particle without crystallization using the X-ray free-electron laser, but in practice it is not yet possible to do so.
the X-ray free-electron-laser technique is a powerful new tool that will be of considerable importance for structural biology in the future.
the use of triple correlation functions is the most powerful and efficient approach for determining the sign of expansion coefficients of the diffraction volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new approach to determine the sign of the Fourier coefficients of a virus structure, which is based on triple correlations between the diffraction volume of the virus and a set of reference structures.

the use of triple correlations for sign determinations of coefficients for symmetric approximations to diffraction volumes can be a very useful approach in the determination of structures of biological particles.

the use of triple correlations for sign determination of the expansion coefficients of a symmetric approximation to a virus structure can be used to determine the structure of a virus to a precision of about 1 Å.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the symmetry of a virus can be used to find the sign determinations (i.e., whether an expansion coefficient is positive or negative) of the Fourier coefficients of the diffraction volumes, which is a key part of the determination of the phase problem of crystallography.
the use of triple correlations can provide a sign determination of the expansion coefficients of the diffraction volume of the virus, and thus a sign determination of its structure.
the sign of a Fourier coefficient can be determined from a triple correlation of the measured intensities.
